new_spots.name: Dog Stream Waterfall
new_spots.photo_reason: No photo proposed; none found on Commons. Acceptable to ship without one (flag for a later photo pass). DOC Waterfall Track page loaded: 41 m Dog Stream waterfall, 2.1 km / 1h30 one way from Mullans Road carpark, Spur Track loop; bio and 2.5-3.5 h visit time match. Coordinates (-42.490, 172.841) sit ~3.8 km NNE of the village in Hanmer Forest Park, consistent with DOC access description; Nominatim/Overpass were rate-limited so only checked by Commons geosearch and DOC text. ticketUrl is DOC's own page for the track; acceptable as the managing agency's page.

new_spots.name: Mount Isobel
new_spots.photo_reason: Fails IMAGES.md check 3 and size: 2008 Nikon Coolpix 990 shot, 1024 px wide (under 1280 minimum), mountain is small and hazy with a green patio umbrella and conifers dominating the foreground and village roofs below; reads as a snapshot from a terrace, not a spectacular view. Subject is correct (right place, the peak is shown). Set photo to null or find a sharper peak photo. Also wiki: 'Mount Isobel' has no English Wikipedia article (verified missing), so wiki should be null; coordinates match Commons Category:Mount Isobel (-42.482, 172.848) and Wikidata Q30508732 'mountain near Hanmer Springs'. Wikipedia Hanmer Springs article states 1,324 m and Jacks/Jollies Pass access; DOC Waterfall Track page also references the Mt Isobel Track. Long hike but named by Wikipedia, DOC and a guide: qualifies.

new_spots.name: Queen Mary Hospital
new_spots.bio_fix: A former soldiers' hospital opened in 1916 beside the thermal pools, whose Soldiers' Block, Nurses' Home and Chisholm Block are Category I heritage buildings; the restored Soldiers' Block is being turned into a museum.
new_spots.photo_reason: Passes all four checks: 2019 colour photo, correct place (Commons categories Former hospitals in New Zealand, Hanmer Springs), shows the long white single-storey hospital building itself (the attraction), real photograph, 1968 px wide, well lit, subject centred. Bio error: 'now owned by DOC' is wrong. Per Wikipedia, DOC held the land only 2008-2010; Hurunui District Council has owned it since 2010 and bought the remainder in 2023. Fix bio as given (avoid claiming current ownership). Coordinates match Wikipedia (-42.5236, 172.8278), next to the pools. Qualifies via Wikipedia article, Heritage NZ listing and a guide; visitor-facing (reserve is open to walk through, Soldiers' Block reopened to the public per Wikipedia). Consider hours text 'Exterior viewable from the thermal reserve' as still fair; costs unverified so free:null is fine.

new_spots.name: Lewis Pass
new_spots.photo_reason: Passes all four checks: 2017 colour photo of the alpine tarn on Lewis Pass (Commons category Lewis Pass, tagged as quality image), a real ground-level photograph, shows the tarn and mountains that the Alpine Nature Walk bio describes, 2903 px wide, sharp and well lit. Coordinates equal Wikipedia's (-42.3797, 172.4); the saddle is about 39 km WNW of Hanmer by straight line (proposal says ~33 km; immaterial), outside Hanmer's 15 km span so standalone is correct. Bio verified against Wikipedia (907 m, SH7, beech forest, scenic reserve, Alpine Nature Walk loop around tarn). Note: Lewis Pass does have an English Wikipedia article (pageid 998292), so wiki should be 'Lewis Pass', not null. Valid scenic stop on the Christchurch-West Coast highway that visitors really do stop at.
